scout.title: AI Scout
scout.subtitle: Search a generated world in your own words, read a report whose every line names its row, and compare a pair across ten dimensions with no overall score to hide behind.
scout.askTitle: Ask the scout in your own words
scout.placeholder: e.g. 找一个 22 岁以下、左脚、能踢 CM、预算 2000 万以下的球员
scout.careerHelps: career lets a search rank against the band this club is thinnest in; role adds a fit column and is quoted by the report. Neither is a guess about who you are.
scout.noFilter: No filter came from this sentence — a search over it would rank the whole stored pool.
scout.chooseTwo: choose two candidates with the A and B buttons
scout.noSingleScore: A comparison answers ten dimensions with no composite score — that is the point.
scout.carryQuery: store the sentence I just searched — it is re-applied to every member on each read
scout.noLists: No list yet. A list stores a name, an optional sentence and career, and which players are on it — nothing that measures a player, so nothing here can go out of date without saying so.
scout.addFromSearch: Add a player from the search above. Nothing about him is copied into the list, so what you see tomorrow is what the stored row says tomorrow.
scout.transferTitle: What if this career signed him?
scout.transferSubtitle: a projection over {{min}}-{{max}} future fixtures · it writes {{writes}}
scout.selectPlayer: one of the players this search just returned
scout.chooseCareerPlayer: Choose a career and a player. Nothing you do here moves a player, spends a budget, or reaches a seller — that is what makes the answer a projection rather than a decision.
scout.elevenUnchanged: the eleven does not change — he would be a squad addition, not a starter
scout.fixturesTitle: The fixtures, with and without him
scout.oneSample: One fixture is one sample — a single better result is not evidence of a better side.

career.budgetHelp: This is what the transfer market gets to spend: an offer priced above the balance left is refused. A budget still changes no fixture by itself — only a deal that was actually made changes the eleven.
career.wageBillHelp: Each round the engine plays now costs the career the weekly wage of every deal it holds at the start of that round.

settings.accountUnavailable: Account data is unavailable right now.

settings.exportFooter: GET /progress/export returns plain JSON; the file is assembled and saved by your browser.
settings.featureMapFooter: These switches come straight from GET /capabilities. Anything marked “not built” has no endpoint behind it yet, so no screen fakes it.

settings.accountDescription: This removes the account, its player and training records, AI history, boards, simulations, community posts, shares and uploaded video originals and frames. world.title: Football World
world.description: Browse the generated football world: competitions, clubs, players, fixtures and match reports — every row labelled synthetic, with the seed and method that produced it.
world.lede: One locally generated football world — clubs, squads, fixtures, statistics and reports. Public, browsable, and honest about being invented.
world.contentsEyebrow: What is actually in the tables
world.generationNote: Same seed ⇒ same world. Re-running the generator changes rows that were edited upstream, never the ones that were not, because each row is keyed by a natural key rather than a random identifier.
world.sectionCompetitionsNote: leagues and cups, with tables built from stored results
world.sectionFixturesNote: match centre with the statistics behind the score
world.footerNote: Nothing on this page came from a feed or a scrape: source: synthetic-world, generated from seed {seed} by apps/api/app/services/world. No real club, league or person is represented.
world.unavailableDetail: Start the API with scripts/dev.sh, then reload.
world.emptyNotice: The world tables are empty. Generate them with python -m seed in apps/api, or set WORLD_AUTO_SYNC=true. This page shows nothing rather than placeholder rows.

progress.metaDescription: Your attribute profile, XP level, achievements and the exact reason behind every recorded change.
progress.unavailable: Progress data is unavailable right now.
progress.noSessions: No completed sessions recorded yet. Every number below comes from your onboarding profile only — attributes cannot move until you log training yourself.
progress.profileFooter: All figures read from GET /progress/overview. No modelled or decorative data.
progress.attributesFooter: Selected as the six highest current values in attributes — the API supplies the numbers, the chart adds none.
progress.changesFooter: Read from GET /progress/timeline → attribute_series. Oldest first, newest last.
progress.emptyChangesTitle: No attribute changes in this window
progress.emptyChangesBody: Attributes only move when a session is completed and self-rated. Widen the window or log a session.
progress.emptyAchievementsBody: Achievements are written by the progression engine when a completed session crosses a stored threshold.
progress.howNumbersMoveBody: This engine has no camera, no wearable and no club feed. An attribute only changes when you complete a session and report your own execution and focus; the recorded reason text above is the rule that fired. The AI layer explains and recommends — it never edits your attributes, and every XP award on the history page shows its stored formula.

agents.lede: Six specialists behind one console. Pick an agent for a single answer, or hand the whole task to the orchestrator, which plans the steps, routes each to the agent that owns it and shows every step it took.
agents.questionPlaceholder: Ask, or pick a task below…

tactics.cardWideTitle: Width across the outfield players, in possession.
tactics.cardBehindTitle: Space between this team's back line and its own goal, in possession.
tactics.cardBlockTitle: Mean distance to the nearest team-mate when defending.
tactics.metaDescription: Fifty authored tactical systems — ten shapes times five temperaments — with the width, spacing and space behind the back line measured from their own coordinates, in metres.
tactics.unavailableDetail: The catalogue is stored on boot by apps/api; start it with scripts/dev.sh.
tactics.eyebrow: Authored coaching structures · measured in metres
tactics.lede: Ten shapes × five temperaments = the fifty systems this lab stores. Nothing here is a real team's play: the coordinates are written by this project, and every figure is measured from them.
tactics.metricsTitle: Every figure on this site, and its formula
tactics.metricsNote: These are the in-possession numbers of one row — {name}. Each system's page prints all eight for both phases, and a measure is never printed without the rule that produced it.
tactics.metricsUnavailable: The metrics table needs at least one stored system.
tactics.emptyNote: The catalogue holds {count} rows; the filter is what is empty.
tactics.boardNote: Each card above prints three of its measured numbers; opening a system draws both phases, lists all eight measures with their formulas, and offers the six counterfactuals. The press line sits at {press_line} m and the defending block is {block_depth} m deep — those two authored values are what the out-of-possession board is derived from.
tactics.boardCompareNote: This one is {formation} under {temperament}. Compare the same shape under a different temperament to see the trade: the same eleven players, measured both ways.
tactics.counterfactualNote: Every change is applied to the stored coordinates and the eight measures are recomputed from the result — the answer is never a conclusion kept in a column.
tactics.unknownChange: “{change}” is not one of the {count} changes this lab offers.
tactics.boardBeforeAfterCaption: hollow = before · dashed arrow = the displacement asked for
tactics.appliesTo: Applies to: {targets} · phase: {phase} · {moved} of {total} measures moved.
tactics.clampedNotice: {count, plural, one {# position} other {# positions}} would have left the pitch, so it was clamped to the touchline or goal line rather than moved the full distance. The table below reports where each player actually ended up.
tactics.bothBoardsNote: Both boards carry the same eleven roles. The defending side is not a second drawing: it is the possession board mapped onto a {block_depth} m block whose top edge is the {press_line} m press line.
tactics.isoEyebrow: §13's third view — the same metres, projected
tactics.isoSummary: Show the isometric projection of the in-possession board
tactics.isoNote: Every dot above went through that pair of lines, from the same x/y metres the in-possession board uses — the projection is arithmetic over the board's own numbers, not a second set of coordinates kept in step by hand. Each marker carries the metres it was projected from beside the point it landed on, so the two can be compared without a screenshot. The lawn, the centre circle and the penalty arcs are the 2D frame's own Law 1 measurements, sampled in metres and projected point by point — a circle on the grass is an ellipse here, and computing that ellipse separately would be a second piece of maths to keep in step with the first.
tactics.isoNotNote: What this is not: a rendered scene. There is no camera, no depth buffer and no lighting, so nothing here can show you what a player would see — it is the plan view bent into a diamond, which is what makes it checkable.
tactics.verdictTitle: What this shape is for, and what it costs
tactics.analysisChipTitle: No AI provider key is configured: the text below is assembled from stored passages, not generated.
tactics.analysisEyebrow: {grounded} statements with a passage behind them · {refused} refused
tactics.analysisTitle: What this lab will say about the shape
tactics.refusedEyebrow: Topics this build refused to answer
tactics.refusedNote: The library has no passage that supports these, and retrieval said so. The alternative was a sentence with a source it did not have, which is the one thing this surface is not for.
tactics.demandsEyebrow: The highest demand in the field for each
tactics.demandsTitle: What it asks of a player
tactics.demandsChipTitle: Compared with your player's own tactical attributes on My Football.
tactics.demandsNote: Six tactical attributes, taken as the maximum demanded by any role this shape fields. They are the same six stored on a player, so fit is a comparison rather than an opinion — the page for your own player shows the pairing.
tactics.siblingsNote: Eleven other systems share this shape; each comparison prints all eight measures side by side, with the formula for every one.
tactics.compareMetaDescription: The same eight measurements, computed for two systems from the same phase, side by side.
tactics.compareUnavailableDetail: The comparison reads the stored catalogue; start the API with scripts/dev.sh.
tactics.compareLede: Two authored structures, the eight measurements, and the difference between them. Nothing is averaged across the pair: each side is computed from its own coordinates.
tactics.compareEmptyNote: {count} systems are loaded for the dropdowns. Until both are chosen nothing is computed — an empty comparison would have to invent a row to show you.
tactics.unknownNotice: “{a}” or “{b}” is not a stored system, so nothing was measured. Pick from the list above.
tactics.noindexNote: Both dropdowns are plain HTML with a GET form, so this page is reachable and shareable without JavaScript; it is noindex because a comparison is a question, not a document.
tactics.boardsMetaDescription: Boards you have arranged in the Tactical Lab, with the measurements recomputed from their coordinates.
tactics.boardsLede: A board starts as a copy of one of the 50 authored systems and becomes yours the moment you move a dot. Its measurements are recomputed by the server from the positions you saved, never from the ones still on screen.
tactics.boardsEmptyNote: Pick a system above and copy it — nothing in the catalogue changes when you do.
tactics.boardsPrivacyChip: only you can read these; a share link is per board and revocable
tactics.editMetaDescription: Drag the eleven players, save the arrangement, and share a read-only link.
tactics.editNoNote: No note yet — this board only exists as positions and the measurements taken from them.
tactics.copiedFromNote: Copied from <link>{system}</link>. That system is unchanged: this is a separate row with your coordinates and `data_origin: user`.
tactics.sharedMetaDescription: A board arranged by a FOOTBALL OS account, with the eight measurements recomputed from its saved positions.
tactics.sharedNoNote: The account that arranged this board left no note with it.
tactics.sharedPanelTitle: Both phases as the owner saved them
tactics.sharedOwnerNote: This page cannot be edited, and the account behind it is named only as “{name}”. <link>Browse the 50 authored systems</link> — those are this project's own, with the reasoning written out on each page.
tactics.sharedRevocableChip: shared by link, revocable by the owner at any time
